trailheadDirection: From Seattle on US 2, turn left at Coles Corner and follow that road about 10 miles, then turn right onto White River Road and drive roughly 1.5 miles to a pullout on the left (the winter parking).
approach: From the White River Road winter pullout, follow the short trail past the blue marker beside it; the crag sits on the right side of the road, about 200 feet from the road.
note: Removed 'cross to the right side' (page says only that the crag is on the right of the road); no current closure found; Okanogan-Wenatchee alerts list nothing for White River Road.

trailheadDirection: Take I-90 Exit 38 and follow the road all the way around, passing under the I-90 overpass, to the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead lot; a Discover Pass is needed to park.
approach: From the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead lot, follow the trail (or the fire academy road) over the bridge and bear right, about 15 minutes to the big leaning cedar at the start of Wayne's World. Walk back up beneath Darkside; Erikland is just to the right of Darkside.
note: Exit 38 page ties the Far Side parking to the Dirty Harry's Peak lot; Wayne's World page gives 15 min and the cedar; Erikland page gives cedar then back up under Darkside. Discover Pass stated.

trailheadDirection: From the Mazama store, drive about 3.1 miles up Lost River Road to the Goat Wall Creek drainage and pull off nearby.
approach: From the Goat Wall Creek drainage pullout, hike uphill in the drainage, which narrows and gets brushy. Allow roughly 30 to 40 minutes depending on snow; The Standard is the right-most climb in this area.
note: Only The Standard page backs this walk; Claymore, Goat's Beard Ice and Mazama Queen pages give no access, so appliesTo is The Standard only; approach sentence reworded to say The Standard, not 'the ice climb'.

trailheadDirection: From US 2 at Leavenworth, drive up Icicle Creek Road to the Bridge Creek Campground junction, which is where the road ends in winter.
approach: From the Bridge Creek Campground junction, follow the dirt road over the bridge to a gate on the right, go past it for about 100 feet, then turn uphill to the left toward the falls. The upper half is a steep slope of 30 to 45 degrees that avalanches often.
note: Dropped 'plowed' (page says only that the road ends there in winter); rest matches the Hubba Hubba area page.

trailhead: Dutch Henry Falls trailhead pullout (Jameson Lake Road)
trailheadDirection: From Wenatchee, drive east on US 2 past Waterville and Douglas and the junction with SR 182, then about 8 miles farther turn left on paved Jameson Lake Road; the north trailhead is about 4 miles along on the left, marked by a small preserve sign.
approach: From the Dutch Henry Falls trailhead pullout (Jameson Lake Road), follow the short, easy path through open shrub-steppe to the creek below the falls, where the ice forms; it is about half a mile out and back. The land is a conservation preserve, so no motor vehicles.
note: Half mile is out-and-back per the guide, not one way; only Sundance Kid is shown to be Dutch Henry Falls (Butch Cassidy and Wild Bunch pages have no location), so appliesTo is Sundance Kid.

trailhead: Excelsior Campground road pullout (Mount Baker Highway milepost 40)
trailheadDirection: Drive east on the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) to milepost 40 and park off the pavement on the old road to the closed Excelsior Campground and pump house.
approach: From the Excelsior Campground road pullout (Mount Baker Highway milepost 40), walk back west along the highway to the trail directly opposite milepost 40 and follow it uphill to the crag, staying on the path to spare the moss.
note: MP area page and the guide-service page agree on milepost 40 and the trail opposite it; SR 542 winter-prep closure was MP 48-54 only (Sept-Oct 2026), not at milepost 40.

trailheadDirection: Drive US 2 through Tumwater Canyon to any roadside pullout near milepost 94, where the flow can be seen from the road.
approach: From the US 2 pullouts near milepost 94, find a safe way across the river, which is the main obstacle and may not be frozen at its slow stretches. Follow the bank to the Fall Creek drainage and hike up it through avalanche terrain, about 2 hours from the river to Drury Falls; The Pencil is in the same drainage several hundred yards to the west.
note: 2 hours is from the river, not the road; appliesTo limited to Drury Falls and The Pencil (Comic Book Hero, The Drip, Plastic Fantastic not shown).

trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth on US-2, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and follow it west to Eightmile Campground.
approach: From Eightmile Campground walk a few hundred feet west along Icicle Creek Road, away from town, then turn right and climb the slope to the buttress.
note: Area page Getting There matches; Eight Mile area page agrees; no current closure found (a standing FS order bans parking in marked areas on Eightmile Road 7601).

trailheadDirection: From Seattle take I-90 east to Exit 54 for Hyak, turn right onto WA-906, take the almost immediate left to stay on WA-906, then after about 0.4 miles turn right into the Hyak Sno-Park (winter parking needs a daily fee or seasonal Sno-Park permit).
approach: From Hyak Sno-Park follow the Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail (Iron Horse Trail) south for 3 miles, using the side snowshoe track if on snowshoes. Just before an information board on the left, find a narrow gully on the right, descend beside the creek that runs through the culvert, climbing two short ice steps on the way, and bushwhack through downed trees to the falls, about 50 m off the trail.
note: Fixed the WA-906 turn (almost immediate left to stay on it) and that the two ice steps must be climbed, not just passed.

trailheadDirection: From I-90 take Exit 47 for Denny Creek and follow Forest Road 58 to the three Denny Creek parking lots, about half a mile past the campground (Northwest Forest Pass or Sno-Park permit).
approach: From the Denny Creek parking lots take the Melakwa Lake trail up past Denny Creek to Melakwa Lake, then go up the valley with the flows on your left. A party camped at Upper Melakwa Lake needed under 30 minutes of steep firm snow in winter to reach the base.
note: Parking is half a mile past the campground, not just past it; removed 'northwest side' and 'Line of Fire cliff band' (unsupported); the 30 minutes was from the upper-lake camp.

trailheadDirection: From I-90 Exit 38 follow Homestead Valley Road to Forest Road 9020, just before the road goes under the freeway, and drive about 0.2 miles to a pullout on the right at an old abandoned road.
approach: From the Forest Road 9020 pullout follow the old road south, then west toward the scree field under the wall; it is overgrown now, so expect some bushwhacking. At the scree stay on the road line to a small cut log, then turn uphill on a faint trail to the base of the lower crag. The upper crag sits above it: continue along the base to the west end and take the trail up to the Iron Horse Trail. The walk is roughly 0.2 miles and took one party under 20 minutes.
note: The upper-crag area page itself says go to the Black Ice Crag and climb up to the trail, so the assumption is stated; the walk now says the upper crag is above the lower one, not at the lower base.

trailheadDirection: From Enumclaw drive SR 410 east toward Crystal Mountain to the signed Skookum Falls viewpoint pullout on the right, about 9.5 miles south of Greenwater.
approach: From the Skookum Falls viewpoint pullout cross the White River, the hardest part of the day; how you cross changes year to year. Then scramble the steep, soft slope up to the base of the falls.
note: Route page, area page, waterfall survey (9.5 mi south of Greenwater) and visitrainier agree; FS alerts list no closure at the SR 410 viewpoint (FSR 73 washout is irrelevant to this pullout).
crag: Waterfall ice and mixed routes in the SW Cascades

trailheadDirection: From White Pass drive east on US 12 for about 2.2 miles to Dog Lake and park near it; the Clear Creek Falls overlook lot is likely snowed in during winter.
approach: From the Dog Lake roadside parking (US 12) walk about 10 minutes, with some bushwhacking, to the overlook above the falls, and drop to the creek above the lip. The falls are top-roped or rappelled from there, so the base is reached from above; snowshoes help in deep snow.
note: No page names a 'Dog Lake parking area' (only 'park near Dog Lake'); renamed. The 2.2 miles is a 2004 report's distance from the pass to Dog Lake.
